source: Transit axis. The base rule is COMPUTED in build.py (not stored here): transit is 'free' wherever the entry type is visa-free or freedom-of-movement, because airside transit is strictly less privileged than entry — if you can enter a country without a visa, you can always remain in its international transit area. Every other corridor defaults to 'unknown'.
note: This file holds ONLY the curated exceptions to the base rule, each backed by a cited source (source_page + source_url). 'required' = a transit visa is needed even for an airside connection (the high-value safety case). 'free' = no transit visa is needed despite a non-visa-free entry requirement. It is curated by hand, one corridor at a time, because the Wikipedia transit notes are inconsistent (mostly yellow-fever health notes and Galapagos transit cards); the two largest transit-visa hubs (the United States and the United Kingdom) are not in the captured page set and their rules are conditional on holdings/exemptions, so they are deferred (see 'deferred').

deferred: United Kingdom (GB): Direct Airside Transit Visa (DATV) regime — needed by most nationalities, with a long exemption list and further waivers for holders of US/CA/AU/NZ visas. Conditional on holdings; needs the destination visa-policy page, not in the captured set.

United States (US): C-1 transit visa regime — needed by most nationalities except Visa Waiver Program citizens and existing US visa holders. Conditional on holdings; needs the destination visa-policy page, not in the captured set.

Schengen Area: airport-transit-visa (ATV) list — a specific set of nationalities needs an ATV even airside; the rest may transit airside without one. Destination-level rule; needs a clean citable list before encoding per-corridor.
China (CN): 24/48-hour transit-visa-free scheme for holders of specific third-country visas — conditional on holdings.
